chunks: From him, from Suleyman ibn Hafs, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him), that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)
whenever the guest came to him, would eat with him, and would not raise his hand from the table-spread until the guest raised his hand.

key_terms.رَفْعَ يَدَهُ: Raising his hand (indicating the end of the meal)

ai.seo_question: What is the prophetic etiquette regarding eating with a guest?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from the Ahl al-Bayt chain underscores the Prophetic practice of remaining at the table until the guest finishes, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and active presence in hospitality. It serves as a practical model for hosts to ensure their guests feel valued and attended to, preventing any sense of neglect during the meal.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Suleyman Bin Hafs, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Musa<sup>asws</sup>, that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>,
whenever the guest came over to him<sup>saww</sup>, would eat with him, and would not raise his<sup>saww</sup> hand from the table-spread until the guest raised his hand’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Sulayman ibn Hafs from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother, Musa, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, that when a guest would come to the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause,
he (the Messenger of Allah) would eat with him and would not stop eating before the guest did.’”
